duration.description: Scene length in seconds; no fixed upper limit.

coordinate.description: Position in pixels, measured from the canvas top left. Layers are positioned by their centers.

text.description: Text displayed by a text layer.

file.description: Absolute local file path on the computer running Forma.

time.description: Time in seconds within the scene duration.

inTime.description: When the layer appears, in seconds. It is hidden before this. Changing it trims the clip without moving keyframes.

outTime.description: When the layer disappears, in seconds. Omit it to keep the layer until the scene ends; the scene grows to fit.

trackId.description: Clips with the same trackId share one timeline row, like clips on a video editor track.

post.summary: Inspect the open scene, layer IDs, keyframes, selection, playback, and sampled transforms. Asset data is omitted unless includeAssets is true.

includeAssets.description: Include embedded image/video/SVG data. Usually unnecessary and potentially large.

post.summary: Replace the current project with an empty scene. Inspect or export the existing project first; replace must be true to confirm replacement.

replace.description: Explicitly confirm replacing the current scene.

post.summary: Set scene dimensions, background, or duration. Dimensions change the canvas without scaling layers. Duration cannot truncate existing keyframes.
Add a geometric or text layer and return its ID. Position refers to the layer center. New layers start with one keyframe at t=0; use forma_set_keyframes to animate.

Update a layer name, fill, interpolation, text, or clip timing (inTime/outTime set when it is visible). For animated transforms use forma_set_keyframes. Text can follow a non-text layer using linkId; use an empty linkId to detach.

linkId.description: ID of a non-text layer to follow, or empty string to detach. Offset is derived from the text's current pose.

outTime.description: When the layer disappears, in seconds, or null to keep it until the scene ends. Trims without moving keyframes; the scene grows to fit.

trackId.description: Put the layer on a timeline track shared with other clips, or empty string to give it its own row.

post.summary: Merge complete keyframes into a layer, replacing frames at matching times. Set replace=true to replace all its keyframes. Each frame needs t,x,y,w,h,r,o. Times must be unique and inside the scene duration.

replace.description: Replace the whole keyframe list instead of merging.

keyframes.description: Complete poses in seconds and pixels.

post.summary: Delete a layer after confirm=true. Linked text survives and is detached at its current pose.

Copy a layer. placement=after puts a still copy right after the layer's clip on the same track, pushing later clips right; give it x/y to make the picture jump there, which builds stop-motion sequences. placement=same_time makes an independent copy nudged 20 px, or placed at x/y.

placement.description: Where the copy goes on the timeline.

post.summary: Play, pause, or seek the timeline. Seek pauses playback and requires time. Changes are visible in the open desktop editor.
Render a PNG frame and return it as an MCP image for visual inspection. Does not change the playhead. Preview is scaled down to maxWidth and at most 1600 pixels in either dimension.

Export PNG, static SVG, animated SVG, WebM video, or editable JSON project to Forma's MCP export folder. Returns its absolute path. Filename must be a simple basename with the matching extension; existing files require overwrite=true. WebM records one loop in real time.

format.description: Export format; project means editable JSON.

filename.description: Simple output filename, for example orbit.svg or animation.webm.

overwrite.description: Explicitly allow replacing an existing export.

post.summary: Open an editable Forma JSON file from an absolute local path. Replaces the current scene and requires replace=true. Invalid projects leave the scene intact.

replace.description: Explicitly confirm replacing the current scene.

post.summary: Import a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG file as an embedded layer. SVG is sanitized. Returns its ID for later keyframes. Video layers can be imported through the desktop UI.
